title: India Beat Pakistan by One Wicket in Last-Ball U19 Asia Cup Final
excerpt: Chasing 338 at Al Amerat, India recovered from 252 for eight to finish on 339 for nine off the final ball — Mohit Ulva unbeaten on 49 — and claim a record ninth U19 Asia Cup title.
body:
• India chased 338 to beat Pakistan by one wicket off the very last ball at Al Amerat, Oman, finishing on 339 for nine to win a record-extending ninth U19 Asia Cup title — their first since 2021.
  • Mohit Ulva, batting at No. 10, made an unbeaten 49 off 26 balls and hit the winning boundary off Ahmed Hussain with three runs needed from the final delivery.
  • India were 252 for eight in the 42nd over — 86 needed off 51 balls — before Manal Chauhan (47 off 32) and Ulva added 57 for the ninth wicket and Ulva and Chigurupati Venkata finished the job with an unbroken 30-run last-wicket stand.
  • Pakistan's 337 for nine was built on Usman Khan's 107 and Abdul Qadir's 80, but Kavya Patel (4 for 68) and Venkata (3 for 40) dragged India back into the match late in the innings.
  • Ulva was named player of the match; Aaryavir Sehwag, whose 58 set up the chase, was player of the tournament as its leading run-scorer with 361 runs.

Three runs needed off one ball, one wicket in hand, and a leg-spinner coming in to bowl it. Mohit Ulva, India's No. 10, walked down the pitch to Ahmed Hussain's final delivery and smashed it wide of long-off — one bounce, into the fence — to complete one of the great finishes in junior cricket. India reached 339 for nine in exactly 50 overs at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman on Saturday, beating Pakistan by a single wicket to reclaim the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup and extend their record haul to nine titles.

It was a chase that was lost at least twice — cruising behind a 95-run opening stand, then collapsed to 252 for eight — and when the ninth wicket fell at 309, India still needed 29 off 16 balls with only the last pair at the crease. Ulva and Chigurupati Venkata got every one of them.

Pakistan's 337: Usman's hundred, and a finish that stalled

Pakistan, who won the toss and batted, were carried by their top order. Opener Usman Khan made 107 off 111 balls, with 11 fours and three sixes, and Abdul Qadir counter-attacked with 80 off 54 balls — three fours and eight sixes — in a second-wicket partnership of 135 from 113 balls. Captain Farhan Yousaf added 63 off 60, and at 204 for two after 30 overs, Pakistan had a platform for something well beyond 350.

India's bowlers took the game back at the death. Pakistan managed only 63 runs in their last ten overs while losing six wickets, closing on 337 for nine. Kavya Patel, the right-arm medium-pacer from Gujarat, took four for 68 in his ten overs, and Venkata claimed three for 40 in five — the two bowling performances that quietly decided how steep India's chase would be.

The chase: a strong start, then a collapse

Openers Aaryavir Sehwag and captain Lakshya Raichandani put on 95 for the first wicket. Sehwag, who had been struck on the right forearm by a delivery in the fifth over, batted on with strapping and painkillers to make 58 off 61 balls, according to ESPNcricinfo's match report. Raichandani held the innings together with 80 off 101.

Pakistan's bowlers then choked the middle of the innings. Rizwanullah took three for 53 and Niqab Shafiq two for 57, and wickets fell in clusters — 186 for four became 217 for six in the space of four overs, Raichandani and Anvay Dravid out to consecutive balls. Pakistan's slow over rate brought a penalty that forced an extra fielder inside the circle from the 46th over, but when the eighth wicket fell, at 252 in the 42nd over, 86 were still needed off 51 balls and the final looked finished.

Turning points

  • 10 overs: Pakistan 93 for one — a powerplay that set up their total.
  • 30 overs: Pakistan 204 for two, with Usman and Qadir's 135-run stand in control.
  • Pakistan's last 10 overs: 63 runs, six wickets — the innings India dragged back to keep 338 chaseable.
  • 17.4 overs: Sehwag falls with India 95 for one, ending the opening stand.
  • 36.3 overs: India 217 for six — Raichandani and Dravid out to successive deliveries.
  • 41.3 overs: India 252 for eight. Eighty-six needed off 51 balls, two wickets left.
  • 47.2 overs: Chauhan falls with India 309 for nine. Twenty-nine needed off 16 balls, one wicket left.
  • 50 overs: Ulva's boundary off the last ball seals 339 for nine.

The last two wickets: 87 runs that won a title

Manal Chauhan, a left-handed batting all-rounder from Madhya Pradesh, changed the match. His 47 came off 32 balls, with three fours and three sixes, and his ninth-wicket stand with Ulva was worth 57 runs from 35 balls. When Chauhan was dismissed in the 48th over with the score on 309, India still needed 29 from 16 balls, and the last man, Venkata — already a three-wicket hero with the ball — walked in.

Venkata finished 11 not out off eight balls, but the partnership's arithmetic mattered more: 30 unbroken runs, the strike rotated, no risk taken until the final over. Chauhan later said he had tears in his eyes after getting out, and thanked the support staff for trusting him in the finisher's role. Ulva did the rest.

The final over

Ahmed Hussain, the leg-spinner who finished with none for 38, bowled it. Eight runs were needed; a tie would have taken the final to a Super Over.

The players who decided it

Mohit Ulva — India, No. 10 batter and right-arm medium-pacer

From Surendranagar in the Gujarat/Saurashtra system, Ulva's unbeaten 49 off 26 balls — five fours, three sixes — turned a lost final into a title. He was named player of the match.

Manal Chauhan — India, left-handed batting all-rounder

The 18-year-old from Morena, Madhya Pradesh, who also bowls slow left-arm orthodox, hit 47 off 32 balls and shared the 57-run ninth-wicket stand that made the finish possible.

Lakshya Raichandani — India captain, top-order batter

The Uttarakhand batter, born in Gonda, Uttar Pradesh, anchored the chase with 80 off 101 balls and captained the side to the title.

Aaryavir Sehwag — India opener

The 19-year-old Delhi opener, son of Virender Sehwag, made 58 off 61 despite the forearm blow, and finished as player of the tournament — its leading run-scorer with 361 runs in five matches.

Kavya Patel — India, right-arm medium bowler

The 19-year-old from Mehsana, Gujarat, took four for 68 in ten overs, the best figures of the final, breaking Pakistan's momentum at the death.

Chigurupati Venkata — India, right-arm fast-medium bowler

The Goa bowler took three for 40, then stood at the other end for the entire last-wicket stand, finishing 11 not out off eight balls.

Usman Khan — Pakistan opener

The 18-year-old left-hander from Peshawar made the final's only century, 107 off 111 balls, and for most of the day looked like its defining innings.

Voices

Ulva's explanation of the last ball, at the presentation, was disarmingly simple: "Nothing, I just saw the ball and hit the ball." In his longer post-match comments, he said: "I knew it was my day and I would finish the game," and credited Venkata's running commentary at the other end: "He kept telling me, 'You can do it. You will finish it.'"

Raichandani said the dressing room never gave the chase up: "We were quite optimistic and we didn't stop believing," the captain said. "I always believed in them," he added of the lower order that finished the match.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted on X: "Outstanding day for Indian cricket! Immensely proud of our young cricketers for today's impressive performance and for winning the Men's U-19 Asia Cup 2026. Their success will inspire several youngsters. Best wishes to the team for their endeavours ahead."

Why this one mattered

The win reverses a run of near-misses against the same opponents. Pakistan beat India by three wickets in the group stage on November 8, chasing down India's 208, and thrashed them by 191 runs in the 2025 final in Dubai; Bangladesh took the 2024 title with India as runners-up. India also played this final without pace spearhead Ishan Sood, who missed out with a back niggle, according to PTI.

India's nine U19 Asia Cup titles — 1989, 2003, 2012 (shared with Pakistan after a tied final), 2013–14, 2016, 2018, 2019, 2021 and now 2026 — are the most by any team, and this was their first since 2021.

What's next, and where to watch

No further fixture for this squad has been announced; the next marker for this group is the build-up to the 2028 U19 World Cup cycle, and finishes like Ulva's and Chauhan's will follow them into senior selection conversations. The full highlights package from the final, via Sony LIV, the tournament's rights holder, is embedded above.

To watch the highlights and replays where you are: in India, Sony Sports Network and SonyLIV carried the tournament; in the United States and Canada, Willow TV is the cricket rights holder, with Cricbuzz also listed as a streaming option in broadcast guides; in the United Kingdom, Sky Sports Cricket, Sky Go and NOW carried the coverage; and in the UAE and the wider Gulf, STARZPLAY carried the tournament.
